    Glossary

    🤔 Every term in the guide, decoded. Flip the flashcards and find out how many you know cold.

    • ⏱️ ~10 min
    • 📚 0 sections
    • 🎮 1 interactive
    • ⭐ 145 XP
    • 🔑 1 fragment
    ✏️ sketching an interactive demo…
    Term Meaning
    ACME Protocol for automatically obtaining and renewing certificates (used by Let's Encrypt)
    AEAD Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data: encryption that also detects tampering (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305)
    AES Advanced Encryption Standard, the world's most-used symmetric block cipher
    ALPN TLS extension for choosing the application protocol (HTTP/2, HTTP/1.1)
    Argon2id Recommended memory-hard password-hashing algorithm
    ARQC Authorization Request Cryptogram: the one-time MAC a payment chip computes for each transaction
    ASN.1 / DER The binary structure and encoding used inside keys and certificates
    Associated data Data that's authenticated but not encrypted, like a packet header
    Asymmetric cryptography Public-key cryptography: a public key and a private key
    Attestation A device proving, with a key locked in hardware, which software it booted
    Authentication Proving who someone (or something) is
    Avalanche effect A tiny input change completely changes a hash or ciphertext
    Base64 An encoding that turns bytes into text. Not encryption.
    bcrypt A widely used password-hashing algorithm
    Birthday paradox Collisions appear after about 2^(n/2) tries, not 2ⁿ
    Block cipher Encrypts fixed-size blocks (AES uses 16 bytes)
    Brute force Trying every possible key or password
    CA (Certificate Authority) An organization trusted to sign certificates
    CAA record DNS record listing which CAs may issue certificates for a domain
    CBC Cipher Block Chaining, an older block cipher mode
    Certificate (X.509) A signed document binding a public key to an identity
    Certificate chain Leaf → intermediate(s) → root, each signed by the next
    Certificate Transparency (CT) Public, append-only logs of all publicly trusted certificates
    ChaCha20-Poly1305 A modern AEAD built from a stream cipher and a MAC
    Cipher An algorithm for encryption and decryption
    Cipher suite A named set of algorithms used together in TLS
    Ciphertext Encrypted, unreadable data
    Collision Two different inputs with the same hash
    Constant time Code whose running time doesn't depend on secret values
    CRL Certificate Revocation List
    Crypto agility The ability to swap algorithms without redesigning a system
    CSPRNG Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator
    CSR Certificate Signing Request: a public key plus requested names, sent to a CA
    DEK / KEK Data-Encryption Key / Key-Encryption Key (envelope encryption)
    Differential cryptanalysis Breaking a cipher by tracking how chosen input differences spread to the output
    Diffie-Hellman (DH) The original public key-exchange method
    Digital signature Proof of origin and integrity that anyone can verify with a public key
    DKIM Email standard in which sending servers sign messages
    DMARC Email policy telling receivers how to handle failed SPF/DKIM checks
    DNSSEC Digital signatures for DNS records
    DoH / DoT DNS over HTTPS / DNS over TLS: encrypted DNS lookups
    Double Ratchet Signal's algorithm that gives every message a new key
    DV / OV / EV Domain, Organization and Extended Validation certificate levels
    E2EE End-to-end encryption: only the communicating users can read messages
    ECB Electronic Codebook mode. Insecure; never use it.
    ECC Elliptic-curve cryptography
    ECDH / ECDHE Elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman (ephemeral)
    ECDSA Elliptic-curve digital signature algorithm
    ECH Encrypted Client Hello: hides which website you're connecting to
    Ed25519 A fast, safe signature algorithm on Curve25519
    EMV The chip-card payment standard (Europay, Mastercard, Visa)
    Encoding Changing data format (Base64, hex). Not security.
    Entropy A measure of unpredictability, in bits
    Envelope encryption Encrypting data with a DEK, and the DEK with a KEK
    Ephemeral key A temporary key used for one session and then deleted
    EUF-CMA Unforgeability under chosen-message attack: the standard security goal for MACs and signatures
    Feistel network Cipher design that splits the block in two and mixes one half into the other each round (DES)
    FIDO2 / WebAuthn Standards behind passkeys and security keys
    FIPS US federal standards (e.g. FIPS 197 = AES, FIPS 203 = ML-KEM, FIPS 140-3 = module certification)
    Forward secrecy Stealing a long-term key later doesn't expose past sessions
    GCM Galois/Counter Mode, an AEAD mode for block ciphers
    Hash function A one-way function producing a fixed-size fingerprint
    HKDF HMAC-based key derivation function
    HMAC Hash-based Message Authentication Code
    Homomorphic encryption Computing on encrypted data without decrypting it
    HPKE Hybrid Public Key Encryption, a modern standard (RFC 9180)
    HSM Hardware Security Module: tamper-resistant hardware for keys
    HSTS A header that forces browsers to use HTTPS for a site
    HTTPS HTTP over TLS
    Hybrid encryption Public-key crypto to protect a key + symmetric crypto for the data
    IND-CPA / IND-CCA Security games: ciphertexts reveal nothing even if the attacker can get chosen messages encrypted (CPA) or chosen ciphertexts decrypted (CCA)
    IV Initialization Vector: a starting value for some cipher modes
    JWT JSON Web Token: signed (not encrypted, by default) data for authentication
    KDF Key Derivation Function
    KEM Key Encapsulation Mechanism: a public-key way to create and wrap a shared key
    Kerberos Ticket-based single sign-on protocol behind Windows Active Directory
    Kerckhoffs's principle A system must be secure even if everything but the key is public
    Key The secret value that controls encryption, decryption or signing
    Key exchange Agreeing on a shared secret over an open channel
    KMS Key Management Service (e.g. in the cloud)
    Lattice cryptography Post-quantum cryptography based on hard problems in multi-dimensional grids
    Linear cryptanalysis Breaking a cipher using slightly biased relationships between plaintext, ciphertext and key bits
    MAC Message Authentication Code: a keyed integrity tag
    Malleability Ability to change ciphertext in a way that predictably changes plaintext
    Man-in-the-middle (MITM) An attacker who intercepts and relays communication, impersonating both sides
    Measured boot Recording a hash of every startup stage in a TPM's PCR registers
    Merkle tree A tree of hashes summarizing lots of data with one root hash
    MFA Multi-factor authentication
    ML-KEM / ML-DSA / SLH-DSA NIST's post-quantum key-encapsulation and signature standards
    Mode of operation How a block cipher is applied to data longer than one block
    mTLS Mutual TLS: both client and server present certificates
    Nonce "Number used once": must never repeat with the same key
    Non-repudiation The signer can't credibly deny having signed
    OAEP / PSS Secure padding schemes for RSA encryption / signatures
    OAuth 2.0 Standard for granting an app limited access to an account (authorization, not login)
    OCSP Online protocol for checking whether a certificate is revoked
    One-time pad Perfectly secure cipher with a truly random, single-use key as long as the message
    One-way function Easy to compute, infeasible to reverse
    Onion routing Wrapping traffic in layers of encryption across several relays so no single relay knows both ends
    OpenID Connect (OIDC) Login standard built on OAuth 2.0; issues a signed ID token
    PAKE Password-Authenticated Key Exchange (e.g. SAE in WPA3)
    Passkey A public-key credential replacing a password
    PBKDF2 A password-based key derivation function
    PEM Base64 text format for keys and certificates (-----BEGIN ...-----)
    Pepper A secret added to passwords before hashing, stored separately from the database
    PKCE Proof Key for Code Exchange: makes a stolen OAuth authorization code useless
    PKCS#12 (.p12/.pfx) Password-protected bundle of a certificate, private key and chain
    PKI Public Key Infrastructure: the system of CAs, certificates and rules
    Plaintext Readable, unencrypted data
    Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) Algorithms believed secure against quantum computers
    Preimage resistance Can't find an input for a given hash
    Private key The secret half of a key pair
    Public key The shareable half of a key pair
    Random oracle model Proof technique that treats a hash function as a perfectly random function
    Reduction A proof that breaking a scheme would also solve a problem believed to be hard
    Replay attack Re-sending a previously captured valid message
    Revocation Cancelling a certificate before it expires
    Root CA A self-signed CA certificate trusted directly by devices
    RSA Public-key algorithm based on the difficulty of factoring
    Salt Random, non-secret value making each password hash unique
    SAML XML-based single sign-on standard common in enterprises
    SAN Subject Alternative Name: the names a certificate is valid for
    scrypt A memory-hard password-hashing / key-derivation algorithm
    Secret sharing Splitting a secret so only a threshold of shares can rebuild it
    Secure Boot Each startup stage verifies the digital signature of the next
    Semantic security A ciphertext reveals nothing useful about the plaintext except its length
    Session key A temporary symmetric key for one connection
    SHA-2 / SHA-3 Families of secure hash functions
    Side-channel attack Learning secrets from timing, power, sound or other physical effects
    SNI Server Name Indication: the website name sent in the TLS ClientHello
    SPF Email standard listing servers allowed to send for a domain
    SPN Substitution–permutation network: cipher design of repeated substitution and mixing layers (AES)
    SSH Secure Shell protocol for remote access
    Steganography Hiding the existence of a message inside innocent-looking data
    Stream cipher Encrypts by XORing data with a generated keystream
    Symmetric cryptography The same key encrypts and decrypts
    TLS Transport Layer Security, the protocol behind HTTPS
    TOFU Trust on first use (e.g. SSH host keys)
    Tokenization (payments) Replacing a card number with a substitute number tied to one device or merchant
    Tor The Onion Router: a volunteer network for anonymous browsing using onion routing
    TOTP Time-based one-time password (authenticator app codes)
    TPM Trusted Platform Module: a security chip in PCs
    Trapdoor function A one-way function with a secret shortcut for reversing it
    Trust store The list of root certificates a device trusts
    VPN Virtual Private Network: an encrypted tunnel for network traffic
    WPA2 / WPA3 Wi-Fi security standards
    X25519 Key exchange on Curve25519
    X25519MLKEM768 Hybrid classical + post-quantum key exchange used in TLS
    XOR (⊕) Bit operation: same → 0, different → 1. The core of many ciphers.
    Zero-knowledge proof Proving a statement without revealing anything else
